action:
# Click the “–” (minus) button of the zoom slider in the status bar to reduce zoom level
pyautogui.click(x=1260, y=744, duration=0.5)

# Click the minus button on the bottom-right zoom control to further decrease zoom level
pyautogui.click(x=1255, y=744, duration=0.3)

# Click the small “–” icon on the bottom-right zoom control to decrease the zoom level
pyautogui.click(x=1550, y=1040, duration=0.3)

# Click the "Cancel" button in the “Insert Sheet” dialog to close it
pyautogui.click(x=790, y=566, duration=0.3)

# Click the small “X” close icon at the top-right corner of the “Insert Sheet” dialog to dismiss it
pyautogui.click(x=1310, y=300, duration=0.3)

# Close the “Insert Sheet” dialog by clicking its top-right “X” close icon
pyautogui.click(x=905, y=216, duration=0.3)

# Click the “Cancel” button at the bottom of the “Insert Sheet” dialog to close it
pyautogui.click(x=720, y=565, duration=0.3)

# Close the “Insert Sheet” dialog by pressing the Escape key
pyautogui.press('esc')

# Click the small “–” (minus) icon in the bottom-right zoom control to reduce the zoom level
pyautogui.click(x=1245, y=748, duration=0.3)

# Click the “–” (minus) icon left of the zoom slider in the bottom-right status bar to decrease zoom
pyautogui.click(x=1225, y=747, duration=0.2)

# Click the small “–” (minus) button just left of the zoom slider in the bottom-right status bar to decrease zoom
pyautogui.click(x=1205, y=747, duration=0.2)

# Click the tiny “–” icon left of the zoom slider in the bottom-right status bar to decrease zoom
pyautogui.click(x=1180, y=748, duration=0.2)

# Click the small square “–” icon just left of the zoom slider in the bottom-right status bar to reduce zoom
pyautogui.click(x=1150, y=756, duration=0.2)

# Click the “260 %” zoom percentage text in the bottom-right status bar to open the Zoom dialog
pyautogui.click(x=1330, y=744, duration=0.3)

# Click the tiny “–” zoom-out button at the far bottom-right (≈20 px left of the slider) to decrease zoom
pyautogui.click(x=1175, y=763, duration=0.2)

# Click the tiny “–” zoom-out button at the extreme bottom-right of the status bar to reduce zoom
pyautogui.click(x=1220, y=762, duration=0.2)

# Click the small “–” zoom-out icon directly left of the zoom slider in the bottom-right status bar
pyautogui.click(x=1185, y=756, duration=0.2)

# Hold Ctrl and scroll downward to reduce the zoom level of the spreadsheet
pyautogui.keyDown('ctrl')
pyautogui.scroll(-600)
pyautogui.keyUp('ctrl')
